messages.content: What is the three-layer memory system in DeepTutor?

DeepTutor uses a three-layer memory: L1 is raw event capture (append-only JSONL per surface per day via TraceEvent), L2/L3 are markdown documents with footnote-citation parsing. The MemoryStore class is the public facade; consolidator handles LLM-driven L1→L2 and L2→L3 ops.

expected.notes: Should persist and recall the memory architecture explanation

source_evidence: deeptutor/services/memory/__init__.py:1-12 — docstring describes three-layer subsystem

messages.content: How does the agentic loop work?

The agentic loop in deeptutor/core/agentic/loop.py drives label-driven iteration: each iteration runs a labeled_step, validates the protocol, handles terminal labels (exit), tool labels (dispatch), intermediate labels (preserve context), and protocol violations (retry). LabelProtocol defines the vocabulary.

expected.notes: Should recall explanation of the agentic loop mechanism

source_evidence: deeptutor/core/agentic/loop.py:1-27 — docstring explains label-driven iteration

messages.content: How does tool result truncation work in the CLI?

truncate_for_display in deeptutor_cli/_tool_result.py shows a head of 10 lines by default (DEFAULT_HEAD_LINES), clips long single lines at 240 chars (DEFAULT_LINE_HARD_CAP), and returns (visible_text, hidden_line_count). ToolResultBuffer is a bounded ring of capacity 32 that backs the /show command.

messages.content: What is the research pipeline in DeepTutor?

ResearchPipeline in deeptutor/agents/research/pipeline.py has 4 phases: Phase 1 (Rephrase) uses ask_user tool for clarification, Phase 2 (Decompose) creates an outline of sub-topics, Phase 3 (Research blocks) runs agentic loops per TopicBlock with THINK/TOOL/APPEND/FINISH labels, Phase 4 (Reporting) assembles the final report with citations.
